2. The facts relevant for the disposal of the rule may be stated as follows : —The present opposite party No.1 Sree Narendra Nath Datta instituted a suit being OC Suit No.297 of 1972 in the Court of Munsif (Now Assistant Judge), Sadar, Rajshahi for Specific performance of a contract against one Raghu Nandan Saha on the basis of a bainanama dated 21.5.69 and obtained an ex parte decree on 20.12.73 after causing the alleged service of summons upon the defendants under Order 5 rule 20 of the CPC. Thereafter, the said Raghu Nandan Saha lodged Miscellaneous Case No. 8 of 1974 under Order 9 rule 13 CPC but the said Miscellaneous Case was dismissed On contest by the learned Munsif by his order dated 22.11.74. Against the said order of dismissal, the defendant of that suit preferred an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 41 of 1975 in the Court of District Judge, Rajshahi which was allowed on 31.12.76 after hearing both the sides. The ex parte decree was set aside and the suit was restored to its original file and number. As against the said order of restoration of the suit, the plaintiff of the OC Suit No. 297 of 1972 i.e. the present opposite party No. 1 went up to the Supreme Court but without any result in his favour. Ultimately the present opposite party No. 1 i.e. the plaintiff of OC Suit No. 297 of 1972 obtained a compromise decree on 16.1.81 with the substituted heirs of deceased Raghu Nandan Shaha who meanwhile died. 

 3. Thereafter, the present petitioner i.e. defendant in the earlier suit instituted OC Suit No. 111 of 1981 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi for setting aside the said compromise decree on the allegations of fraud. In the suit he filed an application for examining by a Hand-writing Expert the signature of the executant of the alleged bainanama. A copy of the said application was served upon the other side and the learned Subordinate Judge was pleased to fix 18.8.84 for hearing of the same. On 18.8.84 on behalf of the defendant opposite party No.1 an application was filed for adjournment of the hearing of the application, as his engaged senior lawyer was busy in conducting a trial in the Sessions Court. Of course, some other lawyers were present on half of the defendants but the learned Subordinate Judge rejected the applications for time and took up the matter for hearing and after hearing the parties on the application for expert opinion allowed the prayer of the plaintiff-petitioner by an order dated 18.8.84.
